raw_tool_response: User responded: confirmation_authority=Q6-C01 — CATEGORY AND PRIORITY CONFIRMATION AUTHORITY  1. DOCUMENT CLASSIFICATION AUTHORITY  Introduce a separately assigned, tenant-scoped Classification Reviewer permission.  An authorized Classification Reviewer may: - Accept an AI-suggested document category. - Reject an AI-suggested document category. - Override a suggested document category. - Confirm or override document classification priority. - Provide mandatory reasons for material overrides.  The Classification Reviewer permission is separate from Knowledge Reviewer content-approval authority.  A Knowledge Reviewer must not automatically receive classification approval permissions merely because they can approve document content.  2. SYNTHETIC TICKET CLASSIFICATION AUTHORITY  Support Agents may review and accept or reject AI-suggested synthetic ticket categories and priorities only when explicitly assigned the tenant-scoped Support Classification Review permission.  Support Managers may: - Review disputed classification decisions. - Override synthetic ticket categories and priorities. - Resolve material classification disagreements. - Provide oversight for significant or conflicting classification decisions. - Review escalation recommendations separately.  Support Manager authority over synthetic ticket classification does not automatically confer central taxonomy or document content-approval authority.  3. CENTRAL TAXONOMY AND MAPPING AUTHORITY  The designated Central Taxonomy Governance Owner retains authority to approve changes to common category definitions, priority definitions, and routing mappings.  This authority is distinct from: - Document classification review. - Knowledge content approval. - Synthetic ticket classification review. - Support Manager escalation review. - Tenant account administration.  No tenant-scoped reviewer or Support Manager may independently modify centrally governed taxonomy or mapping definitions.  4. SEPARATION OF DUTIES AND INDEPENDENT REVIEW  - A document submitter must not approve their own document classification decision. - A person must not approve their own restricted classification proposal or override. - Classification decisions must be made by an appropriately authorized reviewer within the relevant tenant. - Material overrides require a documented reason. - The original AI suggestion and previous human-confirmed values must remain preserved. - Rejected or disputed decisions must remain auditable. - If an eligible independent reviewer is unavailable, the decision must remain pending and must not be automatically approved. - Existing independent non-submitter content-approval requirements remain unchanged.  5. EXPLICIT PERMISSION ASSIGNMENT  The following permissions must be independently assignable and tenant-scoped:  - DocumentClassification.Review - DocumentClassification.Override - SupportClassification.Review - SupportClassification.Override - KnowledgeContent.Approve - TaxonomyMapping.Propose - TaxonomyMapping.Approve - Escalation.Review  The exact assignment of these permissions must follow the approved role and governance model.  Possession of one permission must not automatically grant another.  6. ADMINISTRATIVE PRIVILEGE RESTRICTIONS  - Tenant Admin status alone must not grant document classification, content approval, or Support Classification authority. - Platform Admin status alone must not grant tenant-content access or classification approval authority. - Account administration and classification governance must remain separate. - Role assignment must not permit self-escalation or self-approval. - Tenant Admins may request or administer eligible role assignments only within explicitly authorized account-management boundaries. - All permission grants, removals, and changes must be auditable.  7. AUDIT REQUIREMENTS  For every classification acceptance, rejection, or override, record:  - Tenant and relevant document/request reference. - Original AI suggestion. - Previous and final classification values. - Acting user's identity and role. - Exact permission used. - Decision and timestamp. - Mandatory override reason, where applicable. - Relevant taxonomy and mapping version.  8. FIRST-RELEASE DECISION  Adopt separately assigned, tenant-scoped classification permissions.  Document classification, synthetic ticket classification, Knowledge Content Approval, Central Taxonomy Governance, and Support Manager Escalation Review must remain distinct authorities.  Human reviewers may only exercise explicitly assigned permissions within their tenant and authorized scope.  No administrator receives additional classification or tenant-content authority merely through administrative status.  These decisions clarify permission boundaries only. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, external ticket changes, or any bypass of existing Q1-Q5 governance and security restrictions., classification_scope=Q6-C02 — CLASSIFICATION PROCESSING SCOPE AND LIFECYCLE RESTRICTIONS  1. SUPPORTED CLASSIFICATION SCOPE  The first release supports two distinct classification contexts:  A. KNOWLEDGE DOCUMENT CLASSIFICATION  AI category and priority suggestions may be generated for documents undergoing explicitly authorized ingestion and human review.  This includes: - Newly uploaded documents. - Documents undergoing authorized processing. - Draft documents. - Documents pending Knowledge Reviewer approval.  Classification in these states is restricted to the authorized ingestion and review purpose.  B. SYNTHETIC TICKET CLASSIFICATION  AI may suggest categories, priorities, and local queue classifications for synthetic/local-only support tickets or requests within the application.  This capability must not connect to or modify external ticketing systems, CRM records, or support platforms.  Document classification and synthetic ticket classification must remain separate processes with their respective authorization and audit controls.  2. DRAFT AND PENDING DOCUMENT PROCESSING  Draft and pending documents may undergo limited AI classification processing only when:  - The document was received through an authorized ingestion process. - The processing purpose is explicitly classification and human review. - The processing identity has the required tenant-scoped authorization. - The document lifecycle state permits that processing. - Existing security, tenant-isolation, and sensitive-content restrictions are satisfied.  Permitted processing includes: - Category suggestions. - Priority suggestions. - Classification rationale. - Classification-related metadata and review evidence.  Such processing does not constitute document approval, knowledge publication, or retrieval authorization.  3. STRICT SEPARATION FROM AI ANSWER AND ROUTING RETRIEVAL  A successfully processed, indexed, or classified document must not automatically become eligible for AI answers or knowledge-based routing.  Draft, pending, and unapproved documents must remain excluded from authoritative AI answer retrieval and knowledge citation.  Human reviewers may inspect documents only within their separately assigned tenant-scoped permissions and authorized review responsibilities.  Classification suggestions and review metadata must not silently become approved knowledge.  Only independently approved, currently valid, non-expired, non-superseded, non-overdue, and otherwise authorized knowledge may be considered for AI answer retrieval, subject to all existing Q1-Q5 eligibility restrictions.  4. REJECTED, EXPIRED, SUPERSEDED AND OVERDUE CONTENT  The following content must not undergo new AI classification processing or become eligible for AI answer retrieval merely because it remains stored:  - Rejected documents. - Expired documents. - Superseded versions. - Overdue documents pending mandatory 180-day re-review.  Their existing lifecycle and classification metadata may be retained only as permitted by the applicable retention and audit policies.  Any permitted human inspection must remain separately authorized and tenant-scoped.  A corrected or replacement version must enter the normal authorized ingestion, classification, and independent approval process.  5. DELETION-APPROVED CONTENT  Content covered by an approved deletion request must be immediately excluded from:  - AI classification processing. - AI answer retrieval. - AI citation. - New indexing and embedding generation. - New content extraction and derived-content generation. - Classification or routing suggestions based on its deleted content.  Deletion-approved content must not be reprocessed even during an authorized Legal Hold.  Legal Hold may temporarily suspend physical deletion under Q5 but does not restore classification, retrieval, or processing eligibility.  6. CLASSIFICATION AUTHORIZATION AND AUDIT  All classification processing must:  - Remain within the authorized tenant boundary. - Use explicitly permitted processing identities. - Record processing purpose, document reference, lifecycle state, classification result, mapping version, and timestamp. - Preserve original AI suggestions and subsequent human decisions. - Respect separately assigned Classification Reviewer and Knowledge Reviewer permissions. - Avoid exposing document content to unauthorized administrators or other tenants.  A classification-processing permission must not imply permission to approve content or access it for unrelated purposes.  7. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The first release adopts:  - Authorized ingestion/review classification for uploaded, processing, draft, and pending-review documents. - Local synthetic ticket classification suggestions. - Strict separation between classification processing and authoritative AI answer retrieval. - Separate human inspection permissions. - No new AI content processing for rejected, expired, superseded, or overdue content. - Complete exclusion of deletion-approved content from new processing and retrieval. - No automatic approval, publication, or lifecycle-state transition resulting from classification.  8. GOVERNANCE AND REMAINING BOUNDARIES  All Q1-Q5 requirements remain applicable, including:  - Synthetic/local-only and read-only integration boundaries. - Independent non-submitter document approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Tenant-scoped permissions and authorization. - Legal Hold and deletion controls. - Explicit retention decision gates for failed and rejected uploads. - No automatic external actions or integration writebacks.  Any additional processing purpose, content retention, or lifecycle exception requires separate explicit authorization.  These decisions clarify classification processing scope only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, permit unrestricted AI content access, or initiate another process., rationale_deferrals=Q6-C03 — RATIONALE AND REMAINING DEFERRALS  1. FIRST-RELEASE RATIONALE  The first release adopts a controlled classification model that separates AI suggestions, human classification decisions, Knowledge Content Approval, taxonomy governance, and operational ticket actions.  This boundary is appropriate because it provides:  - Consistent classification across tenants. - Explicit human accountability. - Independent approval and review responsibilities. - Auditable classification and override history. - Strict tenant isolation. - Separation between classification processing and authoritative AI answer retrieval. - Protection against unauthorized operational actions.  The first release prioritizes governance, security, traceability, and predictable behaviour over advanced automation and customization.  2. PERMISSION AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES  The following permissions remain conceptually distinct:  - Document Classification Review and Override. - Synthetic Ticket Classification Review and Override. - Knowledge Content Approval. - Central Taxonomy and Mapping Governance. - Support Manager Escalation Review. - Tenant Account and Role Administration.  Permissions must be explicitly assigned and tenant-scoped.  Possession of an administrative role must not automatically grant classification, content approval, or tenant-content access.  The detailed role-to-permission assignment matrix, initial permission provisioning, and operational assignment workflow require explicit authorization and verification before implementation.  Existing non-submitter approval, separation-of-duties, and no-self-approval restrictions remain mandatory.  3. AI PROCESSING AND DATA ACCESS BOUNDARIES  AI classification is limited to authorized ingestion and review purposes.  Draft and pending-review documents may undergo restricted classification processing without becoming approved knowledge or AI-answer eligible.  The processing identity must operate within explicitly authorized tenant and document scopes.  AI processing must not imply unrestricted access to tenant documents, unrelated content, or other tenants' information.  The exact processing service identity, permitted data fields, execution permissions, and technical enforcement details require a separate implementation-level security specification.  No automatic content approval, ticket modification, external writeback, outgoing message, or business action is authorized.  4. SYNTHETIC AND LOCAL-ONLY INTEGRATION BOUNDARY  All first-release ticket and queue classification remains synthetic and local-only.  AI may suggest categories, priorities, queues, and escalation recommendations.  Authorized humans must review and make applicable decisions.  The first release must not: - Connect to external ticketing or CRM systems. - Modify external tickets. - Automatically assign or escalate real tickets. - Send external communications. - Trigger external workflows. - Perform integration-tool writebacks.  Any future external integration requires separate requirements, authorization, and security review.  5. TENANT ISOLATION AND PLATFORM ADMIN RESTRICTIONS  All classification processing, review, decision history, and permission checks must enforce tenant isolation.  Users must only access information within their explicitly authorized tenant and responsibility.  Platform Admin authority remains restricted to platform administration.  Platform Admins must not receive tenant-document content access, document classification approval, Knowledge Content Approval, or unrestricted tenant-data access merely because of their administrative status.  No administrative privilege may bypass Q1-Q5 authorization and lifecycle restrictions.  6. CONTENT HISTORY AND RETENTION DEFERRALS  Content-free classification audit metadata remains subject to Q5's approved 365-day retention policy.  Persistent content-bearing interaction history remains explicitly deferred.  Its permitted content, purpose, access roles, retention duration, deletion rules, and legal-hold handling must be decided separately.  Q5 deletion, backup, retention, and legal-hold obligations remain unchanged.  Classification evidence must not become a mechanism for retaining deleted document content or restoring retrieval eligibility.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS  The following require separate decisions before their affected capabilities proceed:  - Detailed role-to-permission assignment and provisioning matrix. - Technical authorization model for AI processing identities. - Exact permitted document fields and processing scope. - Tenant-specific taxonomy and classification customization. - Advanced classification confidence thresholds. - Persistent content-bearing interaction history and retention. - External ticketing, CRM, and workflow integrations. - Automated ticket assignment and escalation. - Advanced classification analytics and operational SLAs.  Deferral does not imply permission to bypass an existing security, lifecycle, or governance restriction.  8. FINAL FIRST-RELEASE DECISION  The first release will provide controlled, tenant-scoped, human-reviewed classification suggestions for authorized knowledge documents and synthetic/local-only support tickets.  It will preserve independent approval, immutable classification history, explicit permission boundaries, and strict separation between classification and retrieval eligibility.  All Q1-Q5 security, approval, validity, re-review, deletion, retention, and administrative access restrictions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify Q6 requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, permit external integration, or initiate another process.

Their existing lifecycle and classification metadata may be retained only as permitted by the applicable retention and audit policies.  Any permitted human inspection must remain separately authorized and tenant-scoped.  A corrected or replacement version must enter the normal authorized ingestion, classification, and independent approval process.  5. DELETION-APPROVED CONTENT  Content covered by an approved deletion request must be immediately excluded from:  - AI classification processing. - AI answer retrieval. - AI citation. - New indexing and embedding generation. - New content extraction and derived-content generation. - Classification or routing suggestions based on its deleted content.  Deletion-approved content must not be reprocessed even during an authorized Legal Hold.  Legal Hold may temporarily suspend physical deletion under Q5 but does not restore classification, retrieval, or processing eligibility.  6. CLASSIFICATION AUTHORIZATION AND AUDIT  All classification processing must:  - Remain within the authorized tenant boundary. - Use explicitly permitted processing identities. - Record processing purpose, document reference, lifecycle state, classification result, mapping version, and timestamp. - Preserve original AI suggestions and subsequent human decisions. - Respect separately assigned Classification Reviewer and Knowledge Reviewer permissions. - Avoid exposing document content to unauthorized administrators or other tenants.  A classification-processing permission must not imply permission to approve content or access it for unrelated purposes.  7. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The first release adopts:  - Authorized ingestion/review classification for uploaded, processing, draft, and pending-review documents. - Local synthetic ticket classification suggestions. - Strict separation between classification processing and authoritative AI answer retrieval. - Separate human inspection permissions. - No new AI content processing for rejected, expired, superseded, or overdue content. - Complete exclusion of deletion-approved content from new processing and retrieval. - No automatic approval, publication, or lifecycle-state transition resulting from classification.  8. GOVERNANCE AND REMAINING BOUNDARIES  All Q1-Q5 requirements remain applicable, including:  - Synthetic/local-only and read-only integration boundaries. - Independent non-submitter document approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Tenant-scoped permissions and authorization. - Legal Hold and deletion controls. - Explicit retention decision gates for failed and rejected uploads. - No automatic external actions or integration writebacks.  Any additional processing purpose, content retention, or lifecycle exception requires separate explicit authorization.  These decisions clarify classification processing scope only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, permit unrestricted AI content access, or initiate another process.,

rationale_deferrals.exact_rendered_segment: Q6-C03 — RATIONALE AND REMAINING DEFERRALS  1. FIRST-RELEASE RATIONALE  The first release adopts a controlled classification model that separates AI suggestions, human classification decisions, Knowledge Content Approval, taxonomy governance, and operational ticket actions.  This boundary is appropriate because it provides:  - Consistent classification across tenants. - Explicit human accountability. - Independent approval and review responsibilities. - Auditable classification and override history. - Strict tenant isolation. - Separation between classification processing and authoritative AI answer retrieval. - Protection against unauthorized operational actions.  The first release prioritizes governance, security, traceability, and predictable behaviour over advanced automation and customization.  2. PERMISSION AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES  The following permissions remain conceptually distinct:  - Document Classification Review and Override. - Synthetic Ticket Classification Review and Override. - Knowledge Content Approval. - Central Taxonomy and Mapping Governance. - Support Manager Escalation Review. - Tenant Account and Role Administration.  Permissions must be explicitly assigned and tenant-scoped.  Possession of an administrative role must not automatically grant classification, content approval, or tenant-content access.  The detailed role-to-permission assignment matrix, initial permission provisioning, and operational assignment workflow require explicit authorization and verification before implementation.  Existing non-submitter approval, separation-of-duties, and no-self-approval restrictions remain mandatory.  3. AI PROCESSING AND DATA ACCESS BOUNDARIES  AI classification is limited to authorized ingestion and review purposes.  Draft and pending-review documents may undergo restricted classification processing without becoming approved knowledge or AI-answer eligible.  The processing identity must operate within explicitly authorized tenant and document scopes.  AI processing must not imply unrestricted access to tenant documents, unrelated content, or other tenants' information.  The exact processing service identity, permitted data fields, execution permissions, and technical enforcement details require a separate implementation-level security specification.  No automatic content approval, ticket modification, external writeback, outgoing message, or business action is authorized.  4. SYNTHETIC AND LOCAL-ONLY INTEGRATION BOUNDARY  All first-release ticket and queue classification remains synthetic and local-only.  AI may suggest categories, priorities, queues, and escalation recommendations.  Authorized humans must review and make applicable decisions.  The first release must not: - Connect to external ticketing or CRM systems. - Modify external tickets. - Automatically assign or escalate real tickets. - Send external communications. - Trigger external workflows. - Perform integration-tool writebacks.  Any future external integration requires separate requirements, authorization, and security review.  5. TENANT ISOLATION AND PLATFORM ADMIN RESTRICTIONS  All classification processing, review, decision history, and permission checks must enforce tenant isolation.  Users must only access information within their explicitly authorized tenant and responsibility.  Platform Admin authority remains restricted to platform administration.  Platform Admins must not receive tenant-document content access, document classification approval, Knowledge Content Approval, or unrestricted tenant-data access merely because of their administrative status.  No administrative privilege may bypass Q1-Q5 authorization and lifecycle restrictions.  6. CONTENT HISTORY AND RETENTION DEFERRALS  Content-free classification audit metadata remains subject to Q5's approved 365-day retention policy.  Persistent content-bearing interaction history remains explicitly deferred.  Its permitted content, purpose, access roles, retention duration, deletion rules, and legal-hold handling must be decided separately.  Q5 deletion, backup, retention, and legal-hold obligations remain unchanged.  Classification evidence must not become a mechanism for retaining deleted document content or restoring retrieval eligibility.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED IMPLEMENTATION DETAILS  The following require separate decisions before their affected capabilities proceed:  - Detailed role-to-permission assignment and provisioning matrix. - Technical authorization model for AI processing identities. - Exact permitted document fields and processing scope. - Tenant-specific taxonomy and classification customization. - Advanced classification confidence thresholds. - Persistent content-bearing interaction history and retention. - External ticketing, CRM, and workflow integrations. - Automated ticket assignment and escalation. - Advanced classification analytics and operational SLAs.  Deferral does not imply permission to bypass an existing security, lifecycle, or governance restriction.  8. FINAL FIRST-RELEASE DECISION  The first release will provide controlled, tenant-scoped, human-reviewed classification suggestions for authorized knowledge documents and synthetic/local-only support tickets.  It will preserve independent approval, immutable classification history, explicit permission boundaries, and strict separation between classification and retrieval eligibility.  All Q1-Q5 security, approval, validity, re-review, deletion, retention, and administrative access restrictions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify Q6 requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, permit external integration, or initiate another process.
